candidates.name: Tcomp-r-package
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (`Tcomp`, installable via devtools::install_github) that ships the full dataset from the 2011 Tourism Forecasting Competition (Athanasopoulos, Hyndman, Song & Wu, Int'l J. Forecasting 2011): 1,311 time series of tourism-related indicators (visitor numbers, occupancy-adjacent series) across yearly, quarterly ($M1..$M...) and monthly ($M4 etc.) frequencies, stored as R Mcomp/Mdata objects (list `tourism`) rather than CSV. GPL-3.0, 6 stars, last updated 2025-03-20 (actively maintained wrapper around a fixed historical competition dataset).
candidates.why_useful: This is the actual academic tourism-forecasting benchmark (not the well-known Kaggle Airbnb NYC file) with 1,311 real tourism series and both training/holdout splits used for point forecast accuracy competitions — directly on-theme for evaluating our own nights/ADR forecasting methodology against an established out-of-sample discipline (gap #17, methods: nowcasting/backtesting rigor), though the series themselves are generic tourism (arrivals/occupancy), not ABNB-specific.
candidates.geography: Global (multiple countries' tourism organisations, per 2011 competition)
candidates.time_coverage: Data collected for 2010 Kaggle/2011 competition; historical series length varies by frequency (yearly/quarterly/monthly)

candidates.name: Monash Tourism Yearly Dataset (Zenodo, linked from TSForecasting archive)
candidates.what_it_holds: Zenodo record (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.4656103): 518 yearly tourism time series, CC-BY-4.0, ~36.7kB zip, same underlying 2010 Kaggle/2011 IJF Tourism Forecasting Competition data (compiled by Monash University / University of Sydney researchers) reformatted into the Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive's .tsf format. Companion quarterly (zenodo.org/record/4656093) and monthly (zenodo.org/record/4656096) releases exist for the same underlying competition.
candidates.why_useful: The Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive (github.com/rakshitha123/TSForecasting is the code/loader repo, data lives on Zenodo) is the standard reference tourism benchmark used across the forecasting-ML literature; CC-BY-4.0 licensed and machine-loadable via the .tsf reader in the GitHub repo, useful if the team wants a clean point-forecast-accuracy backtesting harness comparable to published tourism-forecasting baselines (gap #17).
candidates.time_coverage: Historical yearly/quarterly/monthly series ending prior to 2010 competition; exact start years not stated on the page
candidates.size_hint: 518 yearly series (companion sets: quarterly + monthly, similar total ~1,311 combined)
candidates.last_activity: Zenodo record created circa 2021 (archive still live)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Same underlying competition data as ellisp/Tcomp-r-package, in a different (.tsf/Zenodo) format with an explicit permissive CC-BY-4.0 license

candidates.name: TSForecasting (Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive)
candidates.what_it_holds: Code/experiment framework (R) for the Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive: loaders for `.tsf` files, forecasting model implementations, evaluation scripts. Datasets themselves are not committed in-repo but pulled one-command from the Zenodo community at zenodo.org/communities/forecasting (which includes the Tourism yearly/quarterly/monthly sets above, plus dozens of other domains: electricity, tourism, traffic, weather, etc.).
candidates.why_useful: Gives a ready-made, citable evaluation harness (train/test splits, standard error metrics) for benchmarking any of our own nowcasting methods against a large, standardized multi-domain time-series archive — useful for the point-in-time / backtesting discipline the project already enforces (gap #17), and as a one-command puller for the tourism .tsf files rather than hand-downloading Zenodo zips.
candidates.license: Not stated on fetched page (check repo LICENSE)
candidates.last_activity: Not captured (active as of Monash archive's ongoing use)

candidates.name: albania-tourism-analytics
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSVs in `data/`: `arrivals_clean.csv`, `air_clean.csv`, `revenue_clean.csv`, `albania_tourism_dataset.csv` — cleaned tourism arrivals, air-transport passenger data, and tourism revenue for Albania, sourced from World Bank and Bank of Albania (quarterly). Analyzed with ML/Streamlit forecasting.
candidates.why_useful: A small but real regional-travel-volume dataset (Balkans/Southeast Europe) with quarterly Bank-of-Albania and World Bank arrivals/air-passenger/revenue series — marginal relevance to ABNB directly (Albania is not a major ABNB market) but fills the general 'regional travel volume outside US/EU' pattern (gap #7) and demonstrates a repeatable World Bank + central-bank pull others could imitate for bigger markets.
candidates.time_coverage: Not fully specified; quarterly Bank of Albania + World Bank series, appears recent (repo updated 2026-03-18)

candidates.name: Turismo_Salento_forecasting
candidates.what_it_holds: `lecce_turismo_pulito.csv`: 760 rows x 27 columns of official Istat (Italian statistics institute) accommodation-movement data — arrivals, overnight stays, Italian vs. international visitor split, and average length of stay by year and municipality — for 92 municipalities in the Province of Lecce (Salento, Puglia), 2014-2024 annual. Also references a separate Naples Airbnb listings snapshot (9,752 listings, Sept 2025) used as a pricing proxy, and uses Facebook Prophet for dynamic-pricing forecasting.
candidates.why_useful: Real, municipality-level Istat tourism-flow data for an Italian region over an 11-year span plus a length-of-stay breakdown by nationality — could support cross-checking European regional-travel-demand patterns (gap #7/regulatory panel already holds Eurostat national-level `tour_ce_omr`; this is sub-national and includes length-of-stay, which Eurostat's monthly series does not break out at this granularity). Airbnb angle is a same-country different-city proxy only, not usable directly for ABNB but the length-of-stay/international-share variables are the more novel piece.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Partially overlaps Eurostat tour_ce_omr already held, but at finer (municipal, length-of-stay/nationality) granularity for one Italian province

candidates.name: tourism-demand-forecast
candidates.what_it_holds: Seasonal forecasting method (method repo, not a novel dataset) for U.S. air-travel demand using public FRED series, with explicit handling of the COVID-19 structural break; claims 1.15% MAPE. MIT license.
candidates.why_useful: FRED is already a held source, but this repo is a working, tested method for building a seasonally-adjusted, structural-break-aware nowcast off FRED air-travel series — could be repurposed as a template/benchmark for our own nights/ADR structural-break handling (COVID-era discontinuities recur in many of our regressors) rather than as new data.
candidates.size_hint: Method repo, no large data files
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: FRED already held as a source; this is a method wrapper, not new data

candidates.name: Tourism-data-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Single committed file `travel_data.xls` used to analyze top tourist-sending and top tourist-receiving countries and trend of the international travel & tourism sector. Exact source, years, and country list not confirmed from the fetched page (needs opening the xls to verify).
candidates.why_useful: Possible bilateral/country-level international-tourist-flow panel (sending vs receiving countries), which would be relevant to cross-border travel-flow proxies (gap #20) if the underlying data turns out to be UNWTO/World Bank sourced and multi-year — but unverified beyond the filename, so flagged as marginal until someone opens the actual .xls.
candidates.last_activity: Not captured (29 stars per topic page, suggesting some traction)

candidates.name: SLTDA-Tourism-Capstone
candidates.what_it_holds: Capstone project using Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) official visitor-arrival statistics for an ML forecasting + Streamlit dashboard; repo has a `/data` folder but exact file names, years, and monthly/annual granularity could not be confirmed from the fetched page.
candidates.why_useful: SLTDA is a genuine national tourism-authority data source (APAC region, gap #7) not currently in our holdings list; worth a follow-up look if someone wants a small additional APAC arrivals series, but unverified as to freshness/granularity and Sri Lanka is a minor market for ABNB.

candidates.name: thailand-tourism-univariate-forecasting-rnn
candidates.what_it_holds: RNN univariate forecasting models benchmarked against traditional methods for inbound tourist demand in Thailand. MIT license, appears method-focused (not confirmed to ship a large novel raw dataset beyond a Thailand-tourism series).
candidates.why_useful: Thailand is a genuine APAC gap-7 market; flagged as low-confidence/low-priority since the underlying data source and its length/committed-file status were not verified via fetch (time budget), but worth a second look if someone is specifically hunting Thailand tourism-authority data on GitHub.

notes: WebSearch was already at its shared 200/200 session budget before this scout ran (0 queries succeeded); DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint returned connection-refused (network-blocked in this environment); Bing via WebFetch returned irrelevant/junk results for site:github.com queries and a clean-but-unrelated tourism page for the second query, then began 429 rate-limiting after a few calls. Fell back to `gh search repos` (used all 4 allotted calls) plus direct WebFetch on specific GitHub/Zenodo/forecastingdata.org pages (not counted against the 4-call limit since those are not search-engine result pages). The 4th gh search ('UNWTO'/'world tourism organization') was polluted by generic repos literally named 'data' and returned nothing on-theme. The clearest, highest-confidence finding is the 2011 Tourism Forecasting Competition dataset (1,311 series), available both as an R package (ellisp/Tcomp-r-package) and as CC-BY-4.0 Zenodo .tsf files via the Monash Time Series Forecasting Archive (rakshitha123/TSForecasting + zenodo.org/record/4656103 and siblings /4656093 quarterly, /4656096 monthly) — this is a well-known academic benchmark, not ABNB-specific, and rates only medium because it's tourism arrivals/occupancy in aggregate rather than STR-specific or point-in-time. Most other GitHub hits for 'tourism demand forecasting' are thin student ML-course projects (single small CSV or Kaggle-scraped file, no committed multi-year panel, several with clearly synthetic/generated data e.g. DILOmcfly/tourism-forecasting's Zermatt series which the author states is 'synthetically generated' — excluded from candidates). Did not find a dedicated 'Kaggle tourism forecasting competition' GitHub mirror distinct from the Monash/Tcomp lineage already covered. Did not find any GitHub repo with a longer/older/point-in-time-vintage tourism series beyond what CONTEXT.md already lists as held (Eurostat, BEA, FRED, Hawaii DBEDT, etc.) — the Albania and Salento repos are the closest to 'new geography, real government data' but are both small and of marginal direct relevance to ABNB. Recommend a follow-up scout specifically targeting 'Kaggle tourism forecasting' dataset mirrors and the M4/M3/M5 competition GitHub orgs (Mcompetitions org on GitHub) which were not directly checked here due to search-tool outages.
